VERDICT: LGTM

The change slots naturally into this controller's established pattern. `OwnerRestControllerV1` already hosts a family of create-time rule helpers that each stream `findAllOwners()` and compare owner fields — `countOwnersRegisteredOn`, `requireCityHasCapacity`, `countNamesakes`, `requireUniqueIdentity`. `flagPossibleDuplicate` is the same shape, placed immediately after `requireUniqueIdentity` (which its javadoc references), and invoked from `addOwner` in the same linear sequence of flag/count setters alongside `setBulkSignupWarning` and `setNamesakeCount`. Logic is in the right unit — this is owner-create business logic that belongs next to its siblings, not a new class.

Reuse is good: it leans on the existing `equalsIgnoreCase` helper rather than re-rolling null-safe comparison, consistent with `countNamesakes` and `requireCityHasCapacity`. Nothing is duplicated — the soft-match concern is distinct from the household/namesake matching. The two new `Owner` fields plus their accessors, and the five schema files / OpenAPI additions, all mirror the existing `bulkSignupWarning` field precisely (column naming, boolean flag + companion id, `readOnly` schema entries). The controller isn't becoming a catch-all here — it already owns this responsibility, and this is one more coherent, additive member of the existing set. A maintainer would find it natural.
